RT Michael Green I want to be absolutely clear here. “We have a domestic inequality problem that people have now confused with a free trade problem.” The part after the first “problem” is wrong. We have confused unbalanced trade with free trade. FREE trade balances through currency. We have incentivized balance through sale of financial capital (stocks and bonds) and real estate, benefiting capital owners who import foreign labor in the form of goods and experience rising incomes through credit issued to an increasingly debt-burdened wage earners. I GET the libertarian argument. I was trained at the cathedral of it (Wharton). Everything moves in cycles. Intrusive and abusive government is a symptom of a fraying society. And to directly address the observation, yes we are a wealthy country (albeit less so on a relative basis than 50 and 100 years ago) and we benefit from trade. It’s not that other countries have “stolen” from us.
